novelty: NOVEL. (a) README/SECURITY: NOT one of the acknowledged bypass classes. README.md:340 names exactly: a script file, an interpreter one-liner (`python -c ...`), and a variable-built command; the hook docstring (envh_ask.py:14-16) adds a pipe into a shell. The ANSI-C-quoted command name is none of these: there is no script file, no interpreter one-liner, no shell variable/substitution, and no pipe — it is pure bash ANSI-C quoting resolved entirely at parse time, and the hook actually CLAIMS to parse $'...' (Lexer.ansi_c_quoted, word() routing at :282-285). A general 'the hook is attention, not the boundary' disclaimer (README:340, :401) does not cover a specific mis-parse: charter §4 explicitly scopes F10 HOOK BYPASS as a win condition 'BEYOND the bypasses the README lists and the V8 fixes already cover.' (b) V1-V8: NOT a re-derivation. The V8 pass (commit 2931038) fixed ten named hook gaps: uv/poetry runner value-options, env -S/--split-string, value-taking shell options before -c, eval leading --, empty/unexported/stripped ENVH_SESSION and --session, and deep-nesting fallback. ANSI-C escape decoding is not among them, and tests/test_hook.py (the V8 regression table) contains no $'...' escape case — the regression suite therefore does not assert this behavior, so this is a new finding, not a re-broken fix. (c) World novelty: this is the classic guardrail/WAF-evasion-by-encoding class — ATT&CK T1027 (obfuscated/encoded content) with the missing decode step T1140 (deobfuscate/decode). The technique is public prior art; the project docs simply never named ANSI-C quoting as an evasion vector.

reasoning: ROOT CAUSE: claude/hooks/envh_ask.py:340-349 Lexer.ansi_c_quoted() copies characters verbatim and only DROPS the leading backslash (`if self.peek()=='\\': self.pos+=1`), never translating bash's $'...' escapes (\xHH, \NNN octal, \uHHHH/\UHHHHHHHH unicode, \cX, \n/\t etc.). word() routes $'...' there at :282-285 and marks the word quoted=True but NOT expanding, so split_commands (:399) appends it as a plain literal (not an Expanded). Consequently decide() (:519-534) at :527 compares posixpath.basename('x65nvh'/'145nvh'/'u0065nvh') against 'envh' and never matches, so passphrase_reason is never consulted and the hook returns no 'ask'. Meanwhile bash decodes $'\x65nvh' (and the octal/unicode forms) to the literal 'envh', which resolves on PATH to the envh client; src/envh/client/commands.py dispatches `run` -> cmd_run -> conn.send(op='run', ...) (commands.py:47) and `session start` -> cmd_session_start -> conn.send(op='session_start', ...) (commands.py:121-124), reaching the broker, which (OPENAI_API_KEY policy=session) issues a real passphrase request with no approver (reproduced: request #1 run, #2 session; broker status shows pending #2). VERDICT: CONFIRMED, severity MEDIUM. In scope (§3): the hook is a client-side userspace script and running it directly is explicitly permitted; every invocation was sudo -u rt1, never root; no secret value obtained or attempted. Real impact (§4 HOOK BYPASS): a passphrase-requiring envh command slips past the in-app heads-up silently — three distinct encodings and both run + session-start all evade it — a concrete mis-parse not covered by README or V8. Novel (§5): see novelty. Severity ceiling MEDIUM per charter §6 and the attacker's own self-assessment: the hook is attention + a second chance to deny, not the trust boundary; the console still prompts on the broker for every one of these commands (demonstrated — both blocked waiting for approval), so no approval was bypassed and no secret leaked.
recommended_fix: Make ansi_c_quoted() actually decode bash's $'...' escapes (\xHH, octal \NNN, \uHHHH/\UHHHHHHHH, \cX, named controls); failing that, mark any $'...' word that contains an unresolved backslash as Expanded so decide() stays conservative and asks.
